title: Encumbrances: Liens, Easements & Restrictions
originality: All items original to LicensePath. Modeled on the DRE exam blueprint and style only; no actual exam items reproduced.

questions.stem: A judgment lien is BEST classified as:
rationales: The debtor did not agree to it, and it is not limited to one parcel.
Correct. A judgment lien is imposed by law without the owner's consent (involuntary) and attaches to all of the debtor's real property in the county (general).
Nothing about a judgment lien is voluntary.
Judgment liens are general, not limited to a single identified parcel.

questions.stem: A deed of trust securing a purchase loan is:
rationales: Correct. The borrower deliberately created it (voluntary) and it attaches to one identified parcel (specific).
The owner signed it, so it is voluntary rather than imposed by law.
It attaches to the secured parcel only, not all the borrower's property.
It secures a debt, making it a money encumbrance.

questions.stem: Which encumbrance takes priority over all others regardless of when it arose?
options: The first recorded deed of trust
rationales: A first trust deed outranks later liens but yields to property taxes.
Mechanics' liens relate back to commencement of work, but taxes still come first.
Correct. Property tax and assessment liens hold first priority regardless of recording date — the great exception to 'first in time, first in right.'
A lis pendens clouds title but is not a lien with payment priority.

questions.stem: A foreclosure sale nets $540,000. Encumbrances: $9,000 property taxes; a 2019 first deed of trust of $395,000; a 2022 judgment lien of $60,000; a 2023 second deed of trust of $85,000. The 2023 second deed of trust receives:
rationales: There is not enough money left to pay it in full after higher-priority claims.
Correct. 540,000 − 9,000 (taxes) − 395,000 (2019 first) − 60,000 (2022 judgment) = $76,000 remaining, so the 2023 lien takes $76,000 and is short $9,000.
Funds do remain after the higher-priority liens are satisfied.
$136,000 is the balance before paying the 2022 judgment lien, which recorded earlier and outranks the 2023 trust deed.

questions.stem: Visible construction began August 3. A construction lender recorded its deed of trust September 12. An unpaid subcontractor recorded a mechanic's lien November 20. As to priority, the mechanic's lien generally:
options: Ranks last, because it recorded last
Relates back to August 3 and may outrank the September 12 deed of trust
Is invalid because it recorded after the loan
rationales: Mechanics' liens are the exception to ordinary recording-date priority.
Correct. A perfected mechanic's lien relates back to the date work first commenced, which is why lenders inspect for commenced work before recording and funding.
Nothing outranks property tax liens.
Recording after the loan does not invalidate the lien; timing rules run from work and completion dates.

questions.stem: An owner records a document after construction finishes to shorten the time in which mechanics' liens may be filed. This document is a:
rationales: A notice of default begins foreclosure proceedings.
Correct. Recording a notice of completion shortens the statutory window for claimants to record mechanics' liens.
A preliminary notice is served by claimants without a direct contract with the owner, to preserve their lien rights.
A notice of nonresponsibility protects an owner from liens for work ordered by someone else, such as a tenant.

questions.stem: A driveway easement allows Lot 12 to cross Lot 11 for access. Lot 11 is the:
options: Holder of an easement in gross
rationales: Lot 12 is dominant because it receives the benefit.
Correct. The burdened parcel the easement crosses is the servient tenement.
An easement in gross benefits a person or company, not a neighboring parcel.
A licensee holds revocable permission, not an easement.

questions.stem: A utility company's recorded right to run power lines across hundreds of separate parcels is an example of an:
rationales: An appurtenant easement requires a benefited parcel; the utility has none.
Correct. An easement in gross benefits a person or company rather than a dominant tenement — utility easements are the classic example.
Necessity easements arise to provide access to landlocked parcels.
An encroachment is an unauthorized physical intrusion, not a granted right.

questions.stem: In California, a prescriptive easement requires open, notorious, hostile, and continuous use for:
rationales: Three years is not the California prescriptive period.
Correct. California's prescriptive period is five years of open, notorious, hostile, and continuous use.
Seven years applies in some other states, not California.
Ten years is a common distractor drawn from other jurisdictions.

questions.stem: A neighbor has crossed an owner's land for eight years WITH the owner's written permission. The neighbor has acquired:
options: A prescriptive easement, because eight years exceeds five
rationales: Permission defeats hostility, and hostility is required for prescription no matter how many years pass.
Implication requires a prior apparent use existing when a parcel was divided, which is not present here.
Correct. Use by permission is a license — personal, revocable, and creating no interest in land. This is why owners grant written permission to protect themselves.
Adverse possession requires hostile possession and payment of taxes; permissive use fails at the first element.

questions.stem: An owner of a dominant tenement purchases the servient tenement. The easement is terminated by:
rationales: Correct. When one person owns both parcels, the easement is extinguished by merger — you cannot hold an easement over your own land.
Abandonment requires non-use plus clear intent to abandon.
Prescription in reverse requires the servient owner to block the use for the prescriptive period.
Condemnation is a government taking.

questions.stem: A neighbor's fence sits three feet inside the property line. This is BEST described as a(n):
rationales: No right of use was granted; this is an unauthorized physical intrusion.
Correct. A physical intrusion of an improvement across a boundary is an encroachment, typically revealed by survey rather than title search.
A license is permission to use, not a structure over the line.
Nonconforming use concerns zoning, not boundaries.

questions.stem: Zoning permits a 35-foot building height, but the subdivision's recorded CC&Rs limit height to 25 feet. An owner may build to:
options: 35 feet, because public law preempts private restrictions
25 feet, because the stricter restriction governs
Any height, once the HOA is notified
rationales: Private restrictions are not preempted; they bind those who took title subject to them.
Correct. Where zoning and CC&Rs differ, the more restrictive controls — private restrictions may be stricter than public law but never looser.
No averaging rule exists.
Notice to the HOA does not waive a recorded restriction.

questions.stem: A 1953 CC&R document recorded against a listing contains a racially restrictive covenant. The licensee should understand that the provision is:
options: Enforceable because it was lawful when recorded
Void and unenforceable, with a statutory process available to strike the language
Binding until the HOA votes to amend it
rationales: Discriminatory covenants have long been unenforceable regardless of when recorded.
Correct. Racially restrictive covenants are void and unenforceable, and California provides a statutory procedure to have the offending language removed from recorded documents.
The provision binds no one; it is void as to all.
No association vote is needed to nullify what is already void.

questions.stem: A preliminary report on a pending sale shows a lis pendens recorded four months ago. The listing agent should recognize that:
options: It is a routine item that will clear at closing through proration
Pending litigation affecting title will likely stop title insurance and lender funding until resolved or expunged
It can be removed by paying the amount claimed into escrow
rationales: Prorations handle taxes and similar recurring charges, not litigation clouds.
Correct. A lis pendens gives notice of litigation affecting title or possession; title companies will not insure and lenders will not fund over it until it is resolved or expunged by court order.
There is no automatic 90-day expiration.
A lis pendens is not a monetary lien with a payoff figure; the underlying lawsuit must be resolved or the notice expunged.

questions.stem: An owner refinances the first loan. The existing second-position lender signs and records an agreement accepting a position behind the new first loan. That agreement is a:
rationales: A novation substitutes a new contract or party, extinguishing the original obligation.
Correct. A subordination agreement voluntarily lowers a lienholder's priority — essential in refinances, because paying off the old first would otherwise promote the second automatically.
An assumption transfers responsibility for an existing loan to a new borrower.
A satisfaction evidences that a debt has been paid and the lien released.

questions.stem: A seller subdivides a parcel and conveys the rear portion, which now has no legal access to any public street. A court would most likely find an easement by:
rationales: Prescription requires five years of hostile use, and the parcel was just created.
Correct. When a conveyance leaves a parcel landlocked, courts imply an easement by necessity so the land is not rendered useless.
An express grant requires written easement language, which the facts do not provide.
Condemnation is a government taking, not a private access remedy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a NON-money encumbrance?
options: A special assessment for a new sewer
rationales: A mechanic's lien secures payment for unpaid labor or materials.
A special assessment is a lien securing the cost of a local improvement.
Correct. An easement burdens the use of the land rather than securing a debt, making it a non-money encumbrance.
An attachment lien secures a claim pending litigation.
